amendment_reason: The one-free-coefficient family had no pair satisfying both frozen auxiliary orders; widen to monic Weierstrass a1,a2,a3 choices while preserving the first census
source: Jacobson et al., Analysis of the Xedni Calculus Attack (2000), section 3.2 Steps 1-7 and Remark 1

base_curve.ordered_pair_law: all distinct nonidentity E(F_47) point pairs

lift_rule.solved_coefficients: a4,a6 uniquely determined over Q from the two lifted point equations when x1 differs from x2

auxiliary_gates.common: x coordinates distinct modulo each auxiliary prime, integral coefficients, good reduction and rank-two Weierstrass incidence rows

coefficient_policy.search: at each auxiliary prime enumerate all residues of a1,a2,a3 in increasing (sum of absolute centered residues, maximum absolute centered residue, centered tuple), take the first good curve with the required group order
coefficient_policy.arm_priority: at 11 search all strict order-6 candidates first, then weak order-7 candidates
coefficient_policy.crt: combine each chosen auxiliary residue and the zero residue at 47 separately for a1,a2,a3; use the centered representative modulo 3619
coefficient_policy.rational_singularity_policy: reject the pair if the selected rational curve is singular; do not search another coefficient tuple

relation.rational_event: Q1+2*Q2=O over Q on the chosen curve

run_cap: complete finite census with all failed and accepted pair rows; no wall-time performance inference
interpretation: Deterministic r=2 CRT curve choice within the monic Weierstrass family; no point CRT or discriminant optimization
